Urea.best_for: Severe Nitrogen deficiency, rapid vegetative leaf growth
Urea.application_tips: Incorporate into moist soil immediately after application or water lightly to prevent nitrogen volatilization as ammonia gas.

DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate).best_for: Root development, seedling establishment, early growth stages
DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate).application_tips: Apply in bands near the seed zone at planting. Avoid direct contact with seeds.

SOP (Sulphate of Potash).best_for: Fruit development, drought resistance, disease resilience, chloride-sensitive crops like Potato and Tomato
SOP (Sulphate of Potash).application_tips: Apply during flowering and fruiting stages. Helps improve fruit quality, shelf life, and water regulation.

MOP (Muriate of Potash / KCl).best_for: General potassium replenishment in non-chloride sensitive field crops like Wheat and Maize
MOP (Muriate of Potash / KCl).application_tips: Apply before sowing or early vegetative stage. Avoid heavy applications on potatoes or tobacco.

Agricultural Lime (Calcium Carbonate).best_for: Raising soil pH when pH is below optimal range (< 5.5 - 6.0)
Agricultural Lime (Calcium Carbonate).application_tips: Broadcast and incorporate into top 6 inches of soil 2-3 months prior to planting for optimal reaction time.

Agricultural Gypsum (Calcium Sulfate).best_for: Improving soil structure and lowering soil pH over time when pH is alkaline (> 7.5)
Agricultural Gypsum (Calcium Sulfate).application_tips: Apply to sodic or compacted clay soils. Helps leach excess sodium without raising soil pH.

Compost / Well-Rotted Manure.best_for: Long-term soil health, microbial activity, moisture retention
Compost / Well-Rotted Manure.application_tips: Apply 5-10 tons/hectare before land preparation. Excellent for improving sandy and heavy clay soils.
